paths.description: Homepage and commerce-feed archetype; covers discovery, product browsing, preferences, responsiveness, privacy, performance and memory.
Search/listing journey; direct shoes query tested to represent result listings.
Cart/checkout entry journey; direct cart route tested as the highest-risk commerce flow.
Account/form archetype; inspected fields, focus and empty-submission behavior.
Public informational/content archetype represented by the resolved brand-assets page.
Unknown URL used to inspect HTTP/not-found recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The interface does not honor the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains white/grey, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces, text, controls and overlays with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: A cookie wall obscures the primary content on every sampled archetype.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, search, cart and brand-assets screenshots all show a large modal covering the page before interaction; on mobile it is clipped.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface that preserves access to essential content, supports light-dismiss where lawful, and never overflows the viewport.

findings.summary: The homepage overflows horizontally on a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured scrollWidth 769px against visualViewportWidth 360px, a 409px overflow; the cookie actions are clipped in the mobile screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop widths, constrain dialogs to 100% of the visual viewport, and use intrinsic sizing/container queries for the product grid and chrome.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and many controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: The active focus probe reported outline:none and no box shadow for input, Continue, role=button controls and links; 34 of the first 50 controls were below 44px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and provide at least 44×44 CSS-pixel hit areas or equivalent spacing for pointer targets.

findings.summary: Representative shopping routes do not preserve a predictable browse-to-buy path.
findings.evidence: Direct search, cart and unknown-route requests all redirected to a generic sign-in page; the originally requested state was unavailable and the consent wall blocked interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep public search and product discovery reachable without account creation, preserve return URLs and cart state, and provide explicit recovery when authentication is genuinely required.

findings.summary: The measured load is slow and main-thread heavy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 14.8s LCP, 7.0s FCP and 500ms TBT (performance 46); the raw-CDP trace independently found five long tasks and 200ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce boot-time JavaScript, split long tasks, and defer nonessential account, analytics and recommendation code.

findings.summary: The initial load ships a large script-heavy dependency graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 214 requests and 3.32MB transferred, including 2.68MB of script, four parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets and several 0/403/424/429 responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused/duplicate bundles, conditionally load authentication and tracking SDKs, consolidate critical CSS and set explicit cache policies.

findings.summary: The rendered interface has multiple accessibility-tree and contrast failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unnamed dialogs, prohibited ARIA, missing required role parents/children, label/name mismatch, invalid list structure and insufficient contrast; accessibility scored 78.
findings.suggestedFix: Give dialogs accessible names, repair role ownership, align visible labels with accessible names, use semantic lists and remediate every reported contrast pair.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and meaningful alternatives.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all 37 images without width/height, 17 without alt and 35 below-fold images without lazy loading; Lighthouse also flagged wrong aspect ratios and low-resolution delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, accurate alt text, loading=lazy below the fold, and resolution-appropriate responsive sources.

findings.summary: The page emits browser errors and blocks platform optimizations.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported console errors, one deprecated API, a BFCache failure, forced reflow and a failed network dependency-tree insight; best practices scored 69.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve console/network errors, replace the deprecated API, remove unload or other BFCache blockers, and batch DOM reads/writes to avoid forced reflow.

findings.summary: Public content is effectively invisible to non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 0% raw/rendered word coverage and classified the response as a JS shell; crawler screenshot is blank. robots.txt is a JavaScript challenge, and Lighthouse flagged invalid robots and canonical signals.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful page content and metadata, serve plain-text robots.txt plus a real sitemap, and emit stable canonical and social/structured metadata per route.

findings.summary: Important browser-enforced security policies are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent. Cookie __tclr lacks Secure and every observed cookie uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict referrer and permissions policies; mark every transport cookie Secure and narrow SameSite where cross-site use is unnecessary.

findings.summary: Third-party and tracking activity dominates the initial request surface.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 145 requests and 2.95MB to third-party origins; the tracker probe found nine third-party origins including Facebook, plus 49 pftk and 22 thtk requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential tracking on consent, remove redundant SDKs, proxy or self-host essential assets, batch analytics and document the purpose/retention of each endpoint.

findings.summary: Core content and machine-readable control files depend on JavaScript challenges.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML contains no content, the crawler view is blank, and both robots.txt and app.webmanifest return challenge HTML. The unknown route redirects to login instead of a useful error state.
findings.suggestedFix: Render core catalog/navigation HTML on the server, return standards-compliant control files without script challenges, and provide resilient 404/offline/retry states.

findings.summary: The sign-in form lacks visible native constraints and input assistance.
findings.evidence: The email/phone input reports required:false and an empty autocomplete token; the attempted empty submission remained blocked by the consent dialog, so actionable validation could not be reached.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an explicit required constraint, suitable autocomplete tokens, validation after interaction, aria-describedby/aria-live error messaging and preserve the entered value on recovery.

findings.summary: Repeated scrolling correlates with substantial retained heap growth.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary had 433,162 nodes/25.64MB; after ten bottom-to-top scroll cycles it had 491,443 nodes/34.54MB, increases of 58,281 nodes and 8.89MB. Separate primitive sessions and route variability reduce confidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Reproduce in one stable session with baseline/target/final snapshots, then inspect retained lazy-list items, observers, closures and caches; release objects when cards leave the live session.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport breakpoints rather than container-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no @container rules while the captured CSS contains many max-width viewport media queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare containment on reusable grids/cards/dialog shells and adapt them with @container queries while retaining a viewport fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome is not declaratively aware of scroll state.
findings.evidence: The long commerce feed has persistent multi-row chrome, but rendered CSS contains no scroll-state container query or scroll-timeline rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce sticky chrome after scrolling and expose position/progress using scroll-state queries or a lightweight declarative progress affordance.

findings.summary: The sampled account entry does not expose phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: The sign-in surface offers email/phone continuation; the form/source probe found no passkey/WebAuthn registration or authentication affordance despite browser support.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in and registration with email/phone recovery, and request any browser permissions only after a clear user action.

findings.summary: The commerce capabilities are not exposed in a structured agent-readable form.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 33, the raw response is an empty JS shell, and the probe found no structured tool surface or machine-readable form metadata beyond rendered controls.
findings.suggestedFix: First server-render product and form semantics, then expose narrowly scoped, confirmable search/cart/account capabilities with agentic forms or WebMCP.

taskList.title: Server-render public catalog content and standards-compliant robots, sitemap, manifest and metadata
Restore predictable public search/cart/error journeys and preserve state across authentication
Reduce boot JavaScript, third-party SDKs, long tasks and render-blocking dependencies
Deploy CSP and complete browser security/cookie policies
Make the consent surface compact, semantic, named and viewport-safe
Repair accessibility semantics, contrast, visible focus and target sizes
Add system-driven dark mode and container-level responsive rules
Resolve console, deprecated API, BFCache and forced-reflow failures
